note: TWO properties that only three ticks through one state file can pin, and the second is a defect caught before it shipped. (1) The baseline is PER-ISSUE: adding #80 to a declared set mid-watch baselines #80 alone and leaves #71's history intact — a per-tick baseline would blind the whole set every time one issue was added, which is fatal for a declaration that changes by design. (2) An issue MISSING from an observation keeps its stored record. `gh issue view` failing produces an observation with no entry for that issue; the first version overwrote the stored items with it, so the next successful tick emitted `issue-first-observation` and SWALLOWED the comment that landed during the outage — a ruling lost to a transient fetch error, on the channel this feature exists to make reliable. A pair fixture cannot reach either property: its `before` would already contain the carried-forward value it was meant to test.

steps.label: #80 is newly declared: it baselines ITSELF, and #71 is not re-baselined
the read of #80 fails: it is absent from the observation, and its baseline must SURVIVE
the ruling lands on #80. It is a DIFF against the surviving baseline, not a first observation
